summary.headline: OnMobile Q2 FY27 revenue rose 3.4% QoQ to INR 128 crore, but management says YoY growth is still negative and ONMO+ revenue is not yet visible.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 3.4% QoQ to INR 128 crore, with Entertainment & Communication at INR 87.7 crore (+3.5% QoQ) and Gaming at INR 40.7 crore (+3.2% QoQ). Gaming subscribers rose 5.4% QoQ to 14.5 million, and EBITDA improved to INR 2.4 crore from INR 1.5 crore. Management said the combined ONMO+ launch spend (marketing, retail network) keeps consolidated EBITDA and PAT depressed, and that external fundraising will be needed in the next quarter. Analysts pressed on YoY decline, subscription growth, ONMO+ pricing, and capital structure, and management gave little numerical disclosure on ONMO+.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 1.5 crore in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.metric: Gaming subscription EBITDA margin (current stage, per CEO)

segments.name: Entertainment & Communication
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 87.7 crore, up 3.5% QoQ and described as stable; includes Tones, videos, master aggregator, Emocion and Buzzmo. Brazil and Ecuador are set to go live for Tones, and a Tones replacement deal with an emerging-market operator is in advanced discussion.

segments.name: Gaming (incl. ONMO+ subscription)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 40.7 crore, up 3.2% QoQ; subscribers up 5.4% QoQ to 14.5 million with growth spread across 20+ operators. Management said it deliberately sacrificed some growth by exiting low-ROI accounts, and that ONMO+ console revenue is not yet visible in reported numbers.

guidance_outlook: Entertainment & Communication revenue growth target of 2-5% for the year, with ~25% EBITDA margin target.
Gaming Subscription growth target of 15-20% for the year, after 30-35% growth last year; EBITDA margin to rise from ~10% to 20-25%.
FY27 ONMO+ revenue expected in the last two quarters, but the biggest impact expected in FY28; combined EBITDA and PAT to stay impacted by ONMO+ launch costs.
Console EBITDA margin guided at 15-25%, depending on whether the company pursues top-50 gaming markets with full retail or a limited B2C plus B2B model.
ONMO+ console price in Spain to rise over time; a EUR 99 yearly price was mentioned as a possible level, and the company says it has flexibility.
Fundraising planned in the next quarter, at parent or subsidiary level, to fund ONMO+ growth into FY28.
capex_capacity: Spain ONMO+ launch: servers in place, boxes arriving the following week, retailers ready for Black Friday launch in late November; over 350 stores to carry boxes, plus an ONMO+ web store in Spanish in November.

India: ONMO+ boxes in about 70 Poorvika stores; Savex distribution deal announced, with rollout across quick commerce, e-commerce and retail starting the following week; Amazon to be added through the Savex arrangement in coming weeks; own website expected live within a couple of weeks.
Spain box requires Spanish-specific inventory with separate codes; cannot reuse India stock.
Tones: new cloud-based platform being rolled out across operators over a few quarters.
demand_pricing: India console entry pack priced at INR 4,999 (three-month box incl. controller and games); Spain priced at EUR 59 versus a PlayStation controller at about EUR 65. A 48-month pack with two controllers is planned at EUR 240 in Spain.
Management declined to disclose units sold, breakeven volumes or subscription renewal rates.
Retail pitched as faster to close (about one-tenth the lead time of a B2B operator deal); operator deals are slow, with broadband providers moving faster than mobile operators.
Two small African operators were lost in the quarter, affecting profitability and some revenue.

B2B talks with telcos in Southeast Asia, Middle East, Africa and Europe; Buzzmo talks with two African telcos, one may go live next quarter. Management expects closures over the next three to five months.

qa_highlights.question: When will YoY growth return, and will FY27 grow, stay flat or decline versus FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: No explicit YoY answer; management said ONMO+ launch investment makes blended EBITDA and PAT limited, and that FY27 will see some ONMO+ revenue with the bigger impact in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Does ONMO+ revenue start in FY27 and will margins improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Some ONMO+ revenue expected in the two remaining FY27 quarters; margins will improve once revenue scales, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why is subscription revenue not growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prioritised profitability, exited inefficient accounts with high marketing cost and collection/currency issues; gaming subscription target remains 15-20% YoY growth, with subscriber growth running above revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ONMO console only on Flipkart and what is the Spain strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Launch on Flipkart was a learning test; Savex deal includes Amazon in coming weeks, website going live in a couple of weeks; Spain uses retail, online ads and store promoters across multiple channels.

qa_highlights.question: Should ONMO+ be separated into subsidiaries with outside capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed the businesses could be separated and said it will meet investors in coming months for funding at OGL or subsidiary level (UAE, India, US, Spain or Europe), with the decision still open; it declined to disclose ONMO+ numbers for strategic reasons.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected on the console?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 15-25% EBITDA margin, depending on whether it pursues top-50 gaming markets with full retail or a limited B2C plus B2B model.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Savex partnership?
qa_highlights.answer: Savex is a large Indian retail distributor (HP, Lenovo, Apple, Meta glasses) reaching over 1,000 retail locations and e-commerce/quick commerce, expected to push the ONMO box across India.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA and PAT remain negative from ONMO+ launch spend; PAT also hit by depreciation on gaming investment.
Fundraising not yet secured; parent cash use is a concern raised by investors, and a subsidiary structure is still undecided.
Subscription revenue growth is slowing and subscriber counts are growing faster than revenue; some accounts are being optimised out.
Unit economics and volumes for console are undisclosed; channel economics (retail vs direct vs partners) are still being tested.
Competitive risk from large global players; Xbox and Nvidia have caps and waitlists, while ONMO+ does not.
Watch Savex and Amazon roll-out timing, Spain Black Friday launch results, and first ONMO+ revenue in Q3/Q4 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on product, retail partnerships and ONMO+ progress, but cautious on near-term financials; management repeatedly deferred ONMO+ numbers and unit data for strategic reasons. Acknowledged dissatisfaction with results and admitted YoY decline without giving a clear FY27 growth number.

I'm not happy with the results overall. When you look at it combined, that's not where we're going, even just the top line.
We're talking about selling in the millions. How much marketing has to be done for getting there?
My answer is going to be it's between a 15% to 25% EBITDA margin.

adds.what: ONMO+ console launch in Spain (boxes, 350+ retail stores, web store) and India (~70 Poorvika stores, Savex distribution)

growth.why: Management guides Entertainment & Communication growth of 2-5% and Gaming subscription growth of 15-20% for FY27, with ONMO+ revenue expected only in the last two quarters, but backing is partial: no ONMO+ units, breakeven or renewal disclosure, and the brief says YoY growth is still negative.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin rose to 52.9% from 51.7% in Q1 and EBITDA improved to INR 2.4 crore from INR 1.5 crore, but gaming subscription EBITDA margin is ~10% against a 20-25% target, and ONMO+ launch spend keeps consolidated EBITDA and PAT depressed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: ONMO+ console capacity is going live now: Spain servers in place with boxes arriving for a late-November Black Friday launch across 350+ stores, and India boxes in about 70 Poorvika stores with Savex rollout starting the following week; first ONMO+ revenue expected in the last two FY27 quarters.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Gaming subscribers rose 5.4% QoQ to 14.5 million and FY27 subscription growth target is 15-20%, but subscription revenue growth is slowing, Q2 revenue was up only 3.4% QoQ, and two African operators were lost.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said it needs real investment in ONMO+ and plans fundraising in the next quarter at OGL or subsidiary level, with the subsidiary structure (UAE, India, US, Spain or Europe) still open, but no capex quantum or unit numbers were disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no raised numbers, YoY revenue is still negative per the brief, and FY27 gaming subscription growth target is 15-20% after 30-35% last year, so upside is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management admitted YoY decline with no clear FY27 growth number, two small African operators were lost in the quarter, and consolidated EBITDA and PAT stay negative from ONMO+ spend while fundraising is not yet secured.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: ONMO+ console launches in Spain (Black Friday, late November 2026) and India (Poorvika, Savex, Amazon via Savex in coming weeks, own website within a couple of weeks), with a 48-month EUR 240 two-controller pack planned in Spain.

rows.label: Buzzmo and Tones B2B deals in Africa and Brazil/Ecuador
rows.why: One Buzzmo African telco deal may go live next quarter, Brazil and Ecuador Tones go-live is set, and a Tones replacement deal is in advanced talks, though management expects closures over the next three to five months.

rows.label: External fundraising at OGL or subsidiary level
rows.why: Management plans fundraising in the next quarter to fund ONMO+ growth into FY28, but the subsidiary structure is undecided and the brief says the raise is not yet secured.

rows.label: ONMO+ console price increase in Spain
rows.why: Management said the Spain price will rise over time, with EUR 99 a yearly price mentioned as a possible level, but Spain entry is currently EUR 59 against a PlayStation controller at about EUR 65.
